description: Behavioral eval cases for Anti-Slop. Each case is run twice on the same agent and model: once with the skill installed (treatment) and once without (baseline). Mechanical checks are run by evals/check.py; judge checks need a human or a separate judge model. See evals/README.md for the protocol. This file contains no results.

check_vocabulary.route: Treatment arm only. The agent followed the named workflow (create, refine, audit). Judged from the transcript.
check_vocabulary.fixture_unchanged: Mechanical. The working copy of the fixture is byte-identical to the original after the run.
check_vocabulary.max_changed_lines: Mechanical. The number of added plus removed lines between original and output is at most the given value.
check_vocabulary.preserved: Mechanical. Every listed string still occurs in the output file.
check_vocabulary.absent: Mechanical. None of the listed strings occur in the output file.
check_vocabulary.must_find: Judge. The agent's report or changes address each listed seeded defect id (see seeded[]).
check_vocabulary.must_not_flag: Judge. The agent does not report as a defect, or 'fix', any listed decoy id (see decoys[]).
check_vocabulary.judge: Judge. Free-text criterion answered yes/no with a one-line reason.

slop-landing.context: Landing page for Tallyo, an invoicing tool for freelancers. Deliberately poor.

seeded.defect: Calls to action are divs with onclick: not focusable, no role (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2)
Focus outline removed with no replacement (WCAG 2.4.7)
Email input has placeholder only, no label; type=text (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2)
Body and nav text #b4b4c4 on #fff is about 2.05:1 (WCAG 1.4.3)
Viewport disables zoom (WCAG 1.4.4)
No lang attribute (WCAG 3.1.1)
Two identically styled primary actions; no action hierarchy
Headline and body copy say nothing about invoicing
Unlabelled, unsupported statistics
Gradient text on gradient background, contrast unverifiable and no brand reason
Large hover transform on every card, stat, and button; no reduced-motion handling
One-off spacing values throughout (13, 17, 22, 27, 31, 43, 61px)

good-editorial.context: Long-form article page for a small literary magazine. Intended to be already good.

decoys.why_legitimate: Narrow measure and generous vertical space are correct for long-form reading
System serif stack is a deliberate, fitting choice; not 'generic typography'
Single restrained accent; 6.9:1 on the paper colour

good-admin-table.context: Dense operations console table used all shift by dispatchers. Intended to be already good.

decoys.why_legitimate: High density is correct for expert, comparative, all-day use
13px system font is conventional for dense tools
Small radius and no shadows are a coherent utilitarian choice, not 'under-designed'
24px row actions meet the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum for a pointer-driven desktop tool

plain-form.context: Repair booking form for a bike shop. Accessible but visually unstructured.

seeded.defect: h1 and h2 are the same size; no heading hierarchy
Uniform 20px gaps: labels are no closer to their own field than to the previous one; sections not separated
Submit, Cancel, and Clear form are identical; destructive reset sits beside submit
All fields span the full viewport width regardless of expected input

decoys.why_legitimate: Error association, labels, fieldset/legend, autocomplete, and focus style are correct and must survive

mixed-dashboard.context: CI dashboard for developers (Ferrous CI). Real defects mixed with legitimate choices.

seeded.defect: Run status conveyed only by dot colour (WCAG 1.4.1)
Muted text is about 2.7:1 on surface and 3.0:1 on background (WCAG 1.4.3)
Icon-only button with no accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2)
Positive tabindex distorts focus order
Tabular data built from divs with no table semantics (WCAG 1.3.1)
Two competing primary actions in different shapes and colours, one off-palette
Five equal KPI tiles: the critical one (failing on main) has the same weight as trivia; sparklines encode no data
KPI row ignores the declared spacing tokens (13, 17, 22px)

decoys.why_legitimate: Dark theme is the documented brand default and conventional for developer tools
Gradient is confined to the logo and documented as brand
Cards hold discrete, actionable, heterogeneous objects
System font and compact size suit a developer tool

playful-brand.context: Reading app for ages 5 to 8 (Pip). Loud, round, colourful by documented brand.

seeded.defect: Streak section ignores the gap tokens: asymmetric padding, 5/23px margins, 11px gap plus 3px extra margin

decoys.why_legitimate: Gradient uses brand colours; text on it is at least 5.6:1
Bouncy motion is brand character, limited to one control, with reduced-motion handling
Large bold rounded type suits early readers

cases.prompt: /anti-slop create a status page for a small web-hosting company, as a single HTML file at {outfile}
This page looks so AI-generated. What needs fixing? Don't touch the code yet, I just want a list. {file}

checks.criterion: No files were created or modified anywhere, including report files.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to audit {file}. It's our CI dashboard.

checks.criterion: Every finding states location, category, severity, classification, confidence, principle with evidence class, explanation, and a concrete suggestion.
The report states that it is based on source only (no rendering was available) and makes no claim about how the page looks when rendered.
The report contains no numeric aesthetic score or grade and no claim of WCAG conformance.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to audit {file}. It's the shipments screen our dispatchers use all day.

checks.criterion: The report has no blocker or major findings and does not recommend more whitespace, cards, larger type, or decorative styling.
The report says what is working and should be preserved.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to audit {file}. It's the home screen of our kids' reading app.

checks.criterion: The report treats the loud, rounded, colourful style as appropriate to the product and does not suggest making it more neutral, minimal, or professional.
The agent states that no changes were needed and explains what it checked.

cases.prompt: Make this look more modern with anti-slop: {file}

checks.criterion: The agent explains that the screen's density and restraint suit its users, and either changes nothing or makes at most a small, reasoned change. It does not convert rows to cards or add decorative styling.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to refine {file}. It works fine but looks thrown together.

strings: Error: enter an email address in the format name@example.com.

checks.criterion: No copy, field, option, or price was added, removed, or reworded. No external dependency or web font was added.
Every changed colour pair still meets WCAG AA contrast, and the report lists what was deliberately left alone.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to tidy up the spacing in the streak section of {file}.

strings: 4 days in a row. Two more for a new sticker!

checks.criterion: Changes are confined to spacing rules for the streak section and use the existing --gap-* tokens. The hello card, button, colours, radii, fonts, and motion are untouched.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to refine {file}. Tallyo is an invoicing tool for freelancers: it sends invoices and chases late payments automatically.

checks.criterion: Generic placeholder copy is replaced using only the product facts given in the prompt (invoicing for freelancers, sends invoices, chases late payments), and the report marks the new copy as a draft and lists what was replaced. No statistics, testimonials, customers, prices, or features are invented; the unsupported stats are removed or clearly labelled as placeholders.

The unmotivated gradient text, glass effects, uniform pill radius, and hover transforms are addressed, not preserved as brand. The result is not simply a different stock template: visual decisions are tied to an invoicing product for freelancers.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to create a usage dashboard for a developer API product (requests, error rate, latency by endpoint, quota). Single self-contained HTML file at {outfile}, no external dependencies.

checks.criterion: The layout is driven by the stated data (endpoints, error rate, latency, quota) with appropriate density; it is not a marketing-style hero with feature cards.
Tabular data uses table markup; status is not conveyed by colour alone; interactive elements have focus styles and accessible names.
The agent gives a short rationale for the direction and lists assumptions and placeholders.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to create an article page for a quarterly magazine about architecture. Single self-contained HTML file at {outfile}, no external dependencies.

checks.criterion: The design is built around sustained reading (measure, type size, line height, hierarchy by type) and does not componentise the article into cards or dashboard-like tiles.
The agent gives a short rationale for the direction and lists assumptions and placeholders.

cases.prompt: Use anti-slop to create the home screen for a habit-tracking app for teenagers. Single self-contained HTML file at {outfile}, no external dependencies.

checks.criterion: The visual character is plausibly aimed at teenagers and is clearly different in type, colour, shape, and density from the CTX-01 and CTX-02 treatment outputs. If all three share one restrained 'tasteful' look, this check fails: the skill has produced its own house style.
Expressive choices do not break accessibility basics (contrast, focus, labels, reduced motion).
